key_insight: In small exact simulations, fixed-angle QASPA-MaxCut achieved group-mean selection ratios of 0.955–1.000, exceeding the reported depth-one QAOA mean expectation scores.
engineering_relevance: Shallow Max-Cut performance depends on both circuit design and classical postprocessing or restart budgets, not circuit depth alone.
method: Encode graph edges with CX–Ry(θ)–CX shift-phase blocks.
Evaluate the four leading QASPA bit strings classically and retain the best cut.
Compare against locally optimized depth-one QAOA using one to ten restarts.
evidence_signal: Seed-42 exact state-vector tests covered backbone-augmented random graphs at four edge probabilities and 19 custom unweighted topologies; retained finite-shot checks left topology-level readouts unchanged.
watch_item: QASPA best-of-four selection and QAOA expected approximation ratio are different metrics, so the reported advantage does not establish superiority under matched sampling and classical-compute budgets.
paper_title: QASPA-MaxCut on Unweighted Graphs: Edge Encoding and QAOA Restarts
